hardware_source: controller hardware DB bundle + fw-update API + tech specs
verification_source: Ubiquiti publishes its device database unauthenticated at https://static.ui.com/fingerprint/ui/public.json, keyed by the same model codes used here and carrying each model's port map, per-interface link negotiation, outlet map, SKU and product name. It is a first-party source for most of this file and is the natural input for a future regeneration. Two limits are worth knowing before trusting it over a product's own specification: it classifies port media coarsely, so a 25G cage and a 10G cage can read alike, and it is occasionally stale -- it understates the Gateway Max as gigabit. Where it and techspecs.ui.com disagree, the published product specification wins. 57 of the models below are absent from it entirely and cannot be checked against it.
corrections: Port media and product names were checked model by model against the source above and the per-product port tables at techspecs.ui.com. Corrected: USG-XG-8's eight 10G SFP+ cages (six had fallen through to the gigabit default, because only the two interfaces carrying an explicit negotiation list were read); Gateway Max, which is 2.5 GbE on every port; Gateway Enterprise's last two ports, which are 25G SFP28 rather than 10G; and the UniFi Gateway Fiber, which carried its raw model code where a product name belongs. On the power line, the management interface is a 100 Mb port on every model but the Power Backup, and six UPS entries gained their product names.
outlet_source: per-model outlet layouts, added separately from the identity and port data above and not regenerated with it. Six models are sourced to public references -- vendor tech specs, the publicly mirrored device-model catalogue, and outlet tables in captured payloads shipped as fixtures by third-party client libraries: USPPDUP, USPRPSP, USPDA2B, USWDA23, USWDA25, and USPRPS, whose entry is a sourced negative (it has no AC outlets, so it carries no outlet table rather than a fabricated one). Three models have no public source and are derived by rule from a sourced sibling, which is weaker evidence and is recorded here as such: USWDA24 and USWDA26 are the EU variants of USWDA23 and USWDA25 and take their layouts unchanged, and USPDA2C extends USPDA2B's layout to its own outlet count. Outlet names on the derived models follow the controller's default naming rather than a captured label. Capability values use the current outlet_caps encoding: public captures for these models predate it and report the legacy form, which sends the controller looking for an outlet_type this emulator does not send.

no hardware reports this code. Ubiquiti's fingerprint DB files it as an alias on the USG product record with an empty sysids list, while real USG hardware identifies as UGW3 (sysid ee21); it has no firmware bundle and no friendly name. Measured against sim controller 10.4.57: it informs and is answered HTTP 404 like any pending device, but the controller never creates a pending document for it -- alone or beside a device that does appear -- and logs nothing about it, while UGW3 and UXGENT adopt to CONNECTED from the same payload branch

controller_version_basis: verified against this build rather than regenerated from it. Every model here was re-checked and none changed type, outlet count, port count or hardware id between the build this catalogue was generated from and this one. The identity and port data therefore still comes from the source named above; the version records what it has been confirmed against.
smart_power_caps_note: Derived from each model's declared capabilities, so a regeneration reproduces it. The two UPS 2U Pro entries are the exception: they carry the higher value a real device was seen reporting, which a derivation cannot reach, and which a regeneration will therefore lower until the overrides file can restate this field.
